subject: Chemistry
title: What Comes After 118?
description: A fast breakdown of What Comes After 118? for builders.

hook.text: Element 119 would start row 8 of the periodic table. Nobody has managed to make it yet.

buildup.text: Japan's RIKEN lab has been trying since 2018, firing titanium beams at curium targets nonstop.

discovery.text: At element 120+, Einstein's relativity warps electron orbits so much that chemistry itself changes.

twist.text: Some theorists predict the table might end around element 172. Beyond that, atoms can't hold together.

climax.text: Finding 119 would prove we can keep pushing nature's limits. The race continues.

punchline.text: Row 8 awaits. The table's next chapter is unwritten.

quiz.question: What makes elements beyond 120 fundamentally different?
options: Relativistic effects warp electron behavior so much that chemistry changes
They would be too large to fit in any container
They would be lighter than hydrogen

details.summary: Scientists are actively attempting to synthesize elements 119 and 120, which would begin the eighth period of the periodic table and enter a predicted region of exotic chemistry..
details.whyItMatters: Elements beyond 118 would test whether the periodic table continues its patterns or breaks down entirely. The chemical properties of eighth-period elements are predicted to violate many established periodic trends.
takeaways: Elements 119 and 120 are the next targets for synthesis by multiple laboratories
Element 119 would begin the periodic table's eighth period for the first time
Relativistic effects may make eighth-period chemistry completely unprecedented

faq.question: What challenges make synthesizing element 119 so difficult?
faq.answer: No combination of available projectile and target nuclei makes element 119 fusion straightforward. The required beams and targets push current technology to its limits. Fusion probabilities are estimated at one successful event per several months of continuous bombardment..

faq.question: Could the periodic table continue indefinitely to higher element numbers?
faq.answer: Theoretically, there may be a limit around element 172 where the atom's electric field becomes strong enough to spontaneously create electron-positron pairs. Practically, elements beyond 120 may have lifetimes too short to detect..
